topic: Competitive/Non-Competitive Inhibition, Feedback Allostery, EC 1–6 Classes, & Holoenzymes
topics: IUBMB Enzyme Classification (EC 1–6: Oxidoreductases, Transferases, Hydrolases, Lyases, Isomerases, Ligases)
Cofactor Classes: Prosthetic Groups (Heme, Biotin), Coenzymes ($\text{NAD}^+$, $\text{FAD}$), Metal Ions ($\text{Zn}^{2+}$, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$)
quickSummary: Competitive inhibitors bind active sites (Km increased, Vmax unchanged; e.g., malonate on succinate dehydrogenase). Non-competitive inhibitors bind allosteric sites (Km unchanged, Vmax decreased; e.g., heavy metals, cyanide). Uncompetitive inhibitors bind only ES complex (Km decreased, Vmax decreased). Feedback inhibition regulates pathways (e.g., isoleucine inhibits threonine deaminase). IUBMB categorizes 6 classes (EC 1–6). Holoenzyme = protein Apoenzyme + non-protein Cofactor (Prosthetic group tightly bound, Coenzyme loosely bound, Metal ion activator).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Competitive: Km increases, Vmax unchanged. Non-competitive: Vmax decreases, Km unchanged. Uncompetitive: both decrease.

conceptBreakdown.content: Chemical inhibitors reduce enzymatic catalytic activity through distinct kinetic mechanisms.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 8.1 Comparative Inhibition Kinetics Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: 8.1 Comparative Inhibition Kinetics Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Inhibition Type | Active Site Competition | Effect on $V_{\max}$ | Effect on $K_m$ | Classic Biochemical Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Competitive** | **YES** (Inhibitor binds free active site) | **Unchanged** (Reversible by adding excess $[S]$) | **Increased** (Apparent affinity decreases) | **Malonate** inhibits *Succinate Dehydrogenase*; **Statins** inhibit *HMG-CoA Reductase* |
| **Non-Competitive** | **NO** (Inhibitor binds allosteric site on $E$ or $ES$) | **Decreased** (Catalytic efficiency ruined) | **Unchanged** (Substrate binding unaffected) | **Heavy metal ions** ($\text{Pb}^{2+}, \text{Hg}^{2+}, \text{Ag}^+$) inhibiting sulfhydryl enzymes; **Cyanide** inhibiting *Cytochrome c Oxidase* |
| **Uncompetitive** | **NO** (Inhibitor binds ONLY to $ES$ complex) | **Decreased** | **Decreased** | **Lithium** inhibiting *Inositol Monophosphatase*; **Glyphosate** inhibiting plant *EPSP Synthase* |

conceptBreakdown.title: 8.2 Allosteric Regulation & Feedback Inhibition
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FEEDBACK INHIBITION CASCADE
                       
 L-Threonine ──[Threonine Deaminase]──► Intermediate A ──► ... ──► L-Isoleucine
      ▲                                                                │
      └─────────────────── [ALLOSTERIC INHIBITION] ────────────────────┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Allosteric Enzymes**: Multi-subunit enzymes exhibiting sigmoidal (S-shaped) saturation kinetics due to subunit cooperativity.
• **Feedback Inhibition**: The accumulated end-product allosterically inhibits the first committed rate-limiting enzyme (*e.g., L-Isoleucine allosterically inhibits Threonine Deaminase*).

conceptBreakdown.content:
### IUBMB Enzyme Classification (EC 1–6)
1. **Oxidoreductases**: Redox reactions (*Dehydrogenases, Oxidases*).
2. **Transferases**: Group transfer (*Kinases, Transaminases*).
3. **Hydrolases**: Hydrolytic bond cleavage (*Esterases, Proteases*).
4. **Lyases**: Cleave bonds without water or redox (*Decarboxylases, Aldolases*).
5. **Isomerases**: Geometric/structural isomer interconversions (*Isomerases, Mutases*).
6. **Ligases**: Join 2 molecules linked with ATP hydrolysis (*DNA Ligase, Synthetases*).

### Holoenzyme Formula
$$\Large \mathbf{\text{HOLOENZYME (Active)} = \text{APOENZYME (Protein)} + \text{COFACTOR (Non-Protein)}}$$

• **Prosthetic Groups**: Tightly or covalently bound organic cofactors (*e.g., Heme in Catalase and Peroxidase, Biotin*).
• **Coenzymes**: Transiently bound organic cofactors derived from vitamins (*e.g., $\text{NAD}^+/\text{NADP}^+$ from Niacin; $\text{FAD}/\text{FMN}$ from Riboflavin; Coenzyme A from Pantothenic acid*).
• **Metal Ion Activators**: Inorganic cations coordinating with active site residues (*e.g., $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ in Carboxypeptidase; $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ in Hexokinase; $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ in Cytochromes*).
